title: The underived exchange morphism is linear on sheaves of modules
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square],
$$
 \begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y,
 \end{array}
$$
let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and, for a scheme $T$, let $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the category of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $u\in\{f,f',g,g'\}$ let $u^{-1}:\Mod(\mathrm{target}_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(\mathrm{source}_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the inverse image of sheaves of modules and $u_*$ the direct image of sheaves of modules, $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; on underlying abelian sheaves they are the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of abelian sheaves. For $G\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ let $\Ex^0_{\square,G}:g^{-1}f_*G\to f'_*g'^{-1}G$ be the underived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] of the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$. Then $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$ is $\Lambda_{Y'}$-linear for the module structures of $g^{-1}f_*G$ and $f'_*g'^{-1}G$ given by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], i.e. it is a morphism of $\Mod(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Consequently the morphisms $\Ex^0_{\square,G}$, $G\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, form a natural transformation $\Ex^0_\square:g^{-1}\circ f_*\to f'_*\circ g'^{-1}$ of functors $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y'_{\Et},\Lambda)$ whose underlying morphisms of abelian sheaves are the abelian underived exchange morphisms. (This is what makes the exchange of Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), available ``on sheaves of modules''.)

proof.text: The two composite ring maps from the constant ring sheaf on Y to the direct images of the constant ring sheaf on X' agree after restriction along the pullback-pasting comparison. Apply sheafification hom-extensionality: the four given constant-section formulas reduce both composites on a constant r to r on X'; naturality of the sheafification unit shows that restriction fixes these constant sections.

Apply Mathlib SheafOfModules.pushforwardComp, pushforwardCongr₂ and pushforwardComp.symm to the ring-map equality. This constructs a natural module isomorphism d : g'_* ⋙ f_* ≅ f'_* ⋙ g_*. Its underlying abelian morphism is Etale.squareLowerStarIso: sectionwise the two sides restrict along the same two pullback-pasting maps, and map_comp_apply identifies their composites.

Take the inverse mate of d.hom under the given compatible module adjunctions g'^{-1} ⊣ g'_* and g^{-1} ⊣ g_*. This is a natural transformation t : f_* ⋙ g^{-1} ⟶ g'^{-1} ⋙ f'_*. The inverse-mate unit identity says that the adjoint of t_G is f_*(unit_{g',G}) followed by d_{g'^{-1}G}. Compatibility of the g' hom-equivalence, evaluated on the identity, identifies the underlying module unit with the abelian unit followed by g'_* of e_gp.inv.

Forget the inverse-mate unit identity. By naturality of squareLowerStarIso, move the g' comparison through this square isomorphism. Etale.unit_map_baseChangeMap_app identifies the resulting unit followed by the square comparison with the abelian g unit followed by baseChangeMap. Compatibility of the g hom-equivalence then gives equality of the abelian adjoints of baseChangeMap followed by f'_* e_gp.inv and e_g.inv followed by the underlying t_G. Injectivity of the abelian adjunction hom-equivalence and cancellation of e_g.inv give the required comparison formula. Naturality is already built into the mate construction.
